A1.justification: Both 38-page PDFs describe the same A-GFN study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-F support reliable comparison. All appendix pages match in extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original A-GFN pretraining and finetuning experiments, molecular property and docking results, ablations, and lead-optimization examples in Sections 6-7 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the A-GFN comparisons in Tables 2-5 and 21-22, ablation plots, and lead-optimization outcomes in Figure 11.

M1.justification: The atomic action space, graph neural network architecture, conditional rewards, TB/MLE pretraining and RTB finetuning procedures are unchanged in Sections 3-5 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ZINC and Enamine molecular data, physicochemical and TDC ADME-T tasks, TPSA-shift scenarios, and five protein targets for molecular generation and lead optimization.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. MolDQN, REINVENT, fragment GFlowNet and Graph MCTS remain in the property-constrained comparisons; the de novo comparator sets in Tables 21-22, including Saturn, also match.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, property ranges, training budgets and sampling procedures are unchanged. Both versions specify the same default 24-hour finetuning budget on a V100, 1,000 evaluation samples for non-binding tasks and 3,000 for binding tasks.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 retains the same dataset-size, temperature, online/offline training and parameter-scaling ablations. The TB-versus-RTB overtraining analysis in Figure 10 and lead-optimization cases in Figure 11 are also identical.

E5.justification: Appendix F.5 retains three A-GFN seeds and selection of the best docking score across three independent docking runs. The seed information in Table 7, uncertainty entries in Tables 21-22 and plotted error bars are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, rankings and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 reports the same 196 A-GFN scaffolds versus 113 fragment-GFN scaffolds in both versions. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The graph and trajectory formulation, Equations 1-8, reward definitions and mathematical metric definitions in Appendix E are unchanged. No formal assumptions, mathematical reasoning or proofs are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about broader chemical-space exploration through atomic generation, inexpensive-reward pretraining, and computational benefits from goal-conditioned finetuning.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same discussions of catastrophic forgetting, RTB's diversity-versus-optimization tradeoff, offline-prior novelty limitations, docking-score biases and future scaling studies. No substantive interpretation or limitation changes.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters and resource disclosures in Appendix C, Table 7 and Appendix F.5 are identical, including the 12-day hybrid and 18-day offline-prior pretraining schedules on four A100 GPUs. No technical or access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. The conclusion's claim concerning the first useful large-scale application of GFlowNet pretraining is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Martin Ester to the author list and Simon Fraser University to the affiliations, and changes Emmanuel Bengio's affiliation from Recursion Pharmaceuticals to Valence Labs. Scientific prose and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author and affiliation block accompanies reflow of the main text and references. Table 4 moves from PDF page 6 to page 7, and Table 5 shifts within page 7. Figures, captions and table structures remain unchanged; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The author and affiliation updates and table reflow leave the scientific argument, experimental support, reproducibility information and limitations unchanged. With the appendices also identical, these limited presentation changes make no meaningful net difference to the paper's overall quality.
